findings.title: Non-root account with UID 0
findings.description: Accounts other than 'root' have UID 0 and therefore full root privileges.

remediation.summary: Verify each account; if unauthorized, lock it (usermod -L) after capturing evidence.

findings.title: Unsafe permissions on sensitive system files
findings.description: Sensitive files should not be writable by group/other (shadow files not readable by other either).

remediation.summary: Restore distribution defaults (e.g. chmod 0644 passwd/group, 0640 shadow, 0440 sudoers) after checking ownership.

findings.title: Shell or netcat process with an established connection
findings.description: An interactive shell or netcat/socat holding a network connection is characteristic of a reverse shell.

remediation.summary: Identify the process tree and remote peer; preserve evidence before containment.

findings.title: Cleartext or unauthenticated admin service reachable on the network
findings.description: Legacy services (ftp, telnet, tftp, r-services, Docker TCP API) listening on a non-loopback address.

remediation.summary: If not required (check scored services first), disable the unit or bind to loopback.

findings.title: Listener owned by a shell, netcat or script interpreter
findings.description: Generic interpreters listening on a socket are a common bind-shell/backdoor pattern.

remediation.summary: Identify the owning process and its parent; preserve evidence before termination.

findings.title: PAM module loaded from outside the system module directories
findings.description: Absolute module paths outside the standard security directories are rare and are used to load credential-capturing modules.

remediation.summary: Hash and inspect the module before removing the rule.

findings.title: PAM authentication can succeed without verifying a credential
findings.description: pam_permit in an auth stack as 'sufficient', or as the only authenticating module, lets any user log in. Debian/RHEL stacks use it only as a final required entry after real checks.

remediation.summary: Compare with the distribution default for this service; restore from the package (e.g. pam-auth-update) after preserving the file.

findings.title: Suspicious cron job
findings.description: Cron entries match reverse-shell, download-and-execute, world-writable-path or similar patterns.

remediation.summary: Preserve the file, then remove or comment the entry after review.

findings.title: /etc/ld.so.preload is populated
findings.description: Libraries listed here are injected into every dynamically linked process; a standard userland rootkit technique.

remediation.summary: Inspect the listed libraries (hash them) before removal.

findings.title: Suspicious shell startup content
findings.description: Profile/rc files run on login or shell start and match reverse-shell, alias-hijack, LD_PRELOAD or similar patterns.

remediation.summary: Preserve the file, then remove the offending lines after review.

findings.title: Suspicious startup script
findings.description: Boot-time scripts match reverse-shell, download-and-execute, world-writable-path or similar patterns.

remediation.summary: Preserve the script, then remove the offending lines after review.

findings.title: Suspicious systemd unit commands
findings.description: Unit Exec/Environment lines match reverse-shell, download-and-execute, world-writable-path or similar patterns.

remediation.summary: Preserve the unit file, then disable it (systemctl disable --now) after confirming it is not a scored service.

findings.title: Suspicious command line
findings.description: Command line matches reverse-shell, download-and-execute or similar patterns.

remediation.summary: Review the process, its parent, and its network connections.

findings.title: Process running from a deleted or memory-backed executable
findings.description: The on-disk binary was removed (or runs from memfd) after launch - typical of fileless or cleaned-up malware, but also of package upgrades without restart.

remediation.summary: Capture evidence (/proc/PID/exe copy, memory) before killing; compare with recent package updates.

findings.title: Process mimics a kernel thread name
findings.description: Command line is bracketed like a kernel thread but the process has a user-space executable.

remediation.summary: Inspect the executable and parent process.

findings.title: Accounts with an administrative primary group
findings.description: These accounts are not listed as group members in /etc/group but hold an administrative group (root, sudo, wheel, admin) as their primary group, which grants the same privileges.

remediation.summary: Verify each account; change the primary group with usermod -g after preserving the passwd and group files.

findings.title: Login-capable account with empty password
findings.description: Accounts with an empty password field may authenticate without a password (subject to PAM/sshd config).

remediation.summary: Set a password or lock the account (passwd -l). Coordinate with scored-service credentials first.

findings.title: Executables modified in the last 3 day(s)
findings.description: Files in bin/sbin directories. Expected after package updates; otherwise a sign of trojanized binaries.

remediation.summary: Verify against package manager checksums (debsums -c / rpm -Va).

findings.title: Connection to a port commonly used by remote-access tooling
findings.description: Remote ports 4444, 4445, 1337, 31337 and 6667 are frequent in default listeners and IRC bots; may be benign.

remediation.summary: Check the owning process and destination.

findings.title: Database, cache, file-sharing or remote-desktop port exposed
findings.description: Data stores and remote-access services are listening beyond loopback.

remediation.summary: Restrict with bind addresses or firewall rules where the service is not meant to be remote.

findings.title: Weak password hashing configured in PAM
findings.description: md5/des/bigcrypt hashes are cheap to crack.

remediation.summary: Use sha512 or yescrypt.

findings.title: PAM rule references a module that is not installed
findings.description: The module is missing from the system module directories; the package may have been removed (a broken stack can lock users out) or the rule may point at planted code.

remediation.summary: Install the owning package or remove the stale rule; verify with the package manager.

findings.title: PAM module files modified recently
findings.description: Replacing a PAM module is a known credential-theft technique; package upgrades also change them.

remediation.summary: Verify against the package manager (see --package-integrity).

findings.title: Process running from a hidden directory
findings.description: Executable path contains a dot-prefixed directory.

remediation.summary: Verify the binary is expected.

findings.title: Failed services
findings.description: Failed units may indicate a broken scored service or a tampered/removed binary.

remediation.summary: Inspect with 'systemctl status UNIT' and 'journalctl -u UNIT'; restore from a known-good package.

findings.title: Failed socket units
findings.description: A failed .socket unit means its service can no longer be activated on demand (for example ssh.socket, cups.socket).

remediation.summary: Inspect with 'systemctl status UNIT'; check for port conflicts or tampered unit files before restarting.

findings.title: Accounts share a UID
findings.description: Distinct account names map to the same UID, giving identical privileges.

remediation.summary: Confirm intent; reassign unauthorized duplicates.

findings.title: System accounts with interactive shells
findings.description: Service accounts normally use nologin/false; interactive shells enable direct logon.

remediation.summary: Set the shell to /usr/sbin/nologin unless the service requires it.

findings.title: Authorized SSH keys for root
findings.description: Direct root key login is a common persistence mechanism.

remediation.summary: Verify each key belongs to an authorized administrator.

findings.title: Authorized keys with forced commands
findings.description: command= options run arbitrary programs on login and can hide persistence.

remediation.summary: Review the command.

findings.title: Sudo rules without password (NOPASSWD)
findings.description: NOPASSWD grants privilege escalation to anyone able to run as those principals.

remediation.summary: Remove NOPASSWD unless required by a scored service.

findings.title: Login accounts whose password never expires
findings.description: Accounts with a usable password and a login shell have no maximum password age, so a stolen credential stays valid until someone changes it. Hashes are not shown.

remediation.summary: Apply 'chage -M DAYS USER' per account once you have confirmed scored-service accounts will not break; rotate known-compromised credentials first.

findings.title: Accounts with an undefined primary group
findings.description: The primary GID does not exist in /etc/group, which is unusual on a managed system and can follow tampering or a removed group.

remediation.summary: Create the missing group or correct the account's primary GID.

findings.title: No account-lockout module in the PAM stack
findings.description: No pam_faillock, pam_tally2 or pam_tally entry was found, so repeated failed logons do not lock an account at the PAM level. sshd rate limiting or fail2ban may still apply and are not detected.

remediation.summary: Enable pam_faillock (deny=5, unlock_time=600) after checking that scored-service accounts cannot be locked out by a flood of bad logons.

findings.title: No password-quality module in the PAM stack
findings.description: No pam_pwquality, pam_cracklib or pam_passwdqc entry and no pwquality.conf settings were found, so password complexity is not enforced by PAM. Other mechanisms (LDAP, SSSD policy) are not detected.

remediation.summary: Install and enable pam_pwquality (or your distribution's equivalent) with a minimum length of 12 or more.

findings.title: Configuration files modified in the last 3 day(s)
findings.description: Compare with your change log.

remediation.summary: Review the diffs where a baseline exists.

findings.title: Libraries or boot files modified in the last 3 day(s)
findings.description: Commonly changed by package updates; shared-library tampering is rare but high impact.

remediation.summary: Verify against package manager checksums (debsums -c / rpm -Va).

findings.title: IP forwarding enabled
findings.description: Forwarding is expected on routers, VPN and container hosts but not on ordinary servers.

remediation.summary: Disable with sysctl if the host is not a router (check container/VPN use first).

findings.title: Non-loopback entries in /etc/hosts
findings.description: Static host entries override DNS and can redirect update or authentication domains.

remediation.summary: Verify each entry is intended.

findings.title: pam_unix accepts empty passwords (nullok)
findings.description: Debian-family defaults include nullok; it matters only if an account has an empty password.

remediation.summary: Remove nullok once no account relies on it (check USR-PWD-001 first).

findings.title: rc.local contains commands
findings.description: /etc/rc.local runs at boot and is a classic persistence location.

remediation.summary: Review its contents.

findings.title: Administrator-defined systemd units
findings.description: 2 service/timer unit(s) outside the vendor directories (and user-level units). Expected for local services; also a common persistence method.

remediation.summary: Confirm each unit is expected.

findings.title: Legacy or high-exposure services enabled
findings.description: Services historically abused or rarely needed (telnet, r-services, tftp, FTP, NFS, SMB, SNMP, Avahi).

remediation.summary: Disable if unnecessary - confirm they are not scored services first.

findings.title: No persistent logging detected
findings.description: No syslog daemon configuration and no /var/log/journal directory were found; with journald's default (Storage=auto) logs may be lost on reboot. Other collectors (agents, remote logging) are not detected.

remediation.summary: Confirm where logs are kept; create /var/log/journal or configure a syslog daemon, and forward logs off the host.

findings.title: World-writable directory mounted without nosuid/nodev/noexec
findings.description: Everyone can write to these directories, so they are where payloads are staged and executed. Mount options that forbid set-ID files, device nodes and execution make that harder. Only separately mounted directories are assessed.

remediation.summary: Add nosuid,nodev,noexec in /etc/fstab and remount. Test first: some installers and scored services execute from /tmp.

findings.title: Kernel tainted by out-of-tree or unsigned module
findings.description: Taint mask 4096 includes out-of-tree (4096) or unsigned (8192) module bits. Legitimate for some drivers; also seen with rootkit modules.

remediation.summary: Review loaded modules (lsmod) against expected drivers.

findings.title: Members of root-equivalent groups
findings.description: docker, lxd and disk group membership is effectively root access.

remediation.summary: Remove members that do not need it.
